text.p: The following are the stories reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
LIETUVOS RYTAS

- The ruling Homeland Union faction in parliament for the tenth time rejected the veto of Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas, stripping him of the right to appoint the prosecutor general and delegating it to a parliamentary committee.
- Ten million litas of state funds were squandered to pay compensations to depositors of the bankrupt Sekunde bank.
- A members of parliament is involved in smuggling, Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said but stopped short of naming him.
- Rokishkis Cheese decided to pay 1.78 million litas in dividends. The company reported 12.2 million net profit in 1996.

- Kaunas textile producer Audimas intends to sign a licensing agreement with U.S. sports gear producer Spalding which would permit the company to use Spalding's name on their products. Spalding products would make up to five percent of Audimas production.
RESPUBLIKA
- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said that national currency litas rate will not change this year.

- Lithuanian parliament approved yesterday the draft law on restoration of lost deposits in state owned banks held before March 1991. The state intends to compensate each litas for one rouble but no more than 6,000 litas to one person.

- Siemens intends to expand its investment in Lithuania, said Siemens Lithuania manager Irja Kamarainen after meeting with economy minister Vincas Babilius. Siemens also wants to open a financial branch in the country.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said that prices for heating will not go up before the end of winter season but did not rule out the possibility that they might go up in the autumn.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said that litas exchange rate changes might be expected in 1998 when the rate could hinge on inflation.
- The major factions in parliament say that the privatisation of the country's strategic companies should be public and controlled by Seimas, the parliament.
VERSLO ZINIOS

- The real income of Lithuanian citizens has increased by 12 percent since 1993 monetary reform but has not yet reached the level of December 1991. The income of the richest Lithuanians is ten times the income of the poorest in the country.

- The net profit of Lithuanian Gas in 1996 was 11 times below 1995 results but the final figures will become known after an international audit carried out by Coopers & Lybrand. The company reported a net profit of 3.9 million in 1996 versus 43.5 million in 1995.
- Ukio bank will propose doubling its share capital to 82 million litas at its general shareholders meeting on March 29.

- The remaining 21,000 shares of Lithuanian Savings bank were sold in 20 minutes. The rush for the shares was because the shares were sold at face value of 100 litas versus 220 litas that they are currently trading at on the bourse.
-- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newroom + 370 2 22 35 17
